subject: Human-authored signed-i64 saturation-clamp mid-end ISLE rewrite, same CLIF compiled with pristine versus one-rule patched x86_64 Cranelift at opt_level=speed_and_size

proof.scope: Pure sign-clamp identity for all signed i64 values; conditional on declared expression semantics, not full ISLE-chain or machine-state correctness

costs.interpretation: ELF function symbol baseline includes trailing data/padding; x86 instruction prefix is a distinct metric, not abstract CLIF or whole-AOT

finite_oracle.oracle: Python arbitrary-precision clamp of x+y into [-2^63,2^63-1]

independent_replay.method: download original Actions artifact; verify archive SHA-256, object hashes, proof/patch receipts, separately run GNU objdump -d -w -Mintel and readelf -Ws on each archived object, link and execute both SysV x86-64 objects against Python oracle
independent_replay.reconstruction: 46 executable instruction bytes over 13 decoded instructions vs 39 over 12; 56 vs 39 full symbol bytes
independent_replay.note: objdump full-text SHA is path-sensitive; independent replay compared object hashes and decoded instructions rather than comparing host-specific dump-header hashes

history.reason: GNU objdump default wrapped long x86 instructions, falsely yielding a disassembly-gap rejection
history.fix: use objdump -d -w -Mintel and preserve strict contiguous address checks

nonclaims: No newly synthesized sequence; rewrite was already human authored
No verified upstream ISLE rule beyond declared pure clamp identity; unchanged upstream VeriISLE specs remain insufficient for this rule
No full physical flags, register allocation, ABI, poison, undefined state, unwinding or machine-code proof
No representative throughput improvement or cross-target profitability
No upstream Wasmtime PR, merge, or general optimization claim
